title: landlord_charged_me_for_the_stairs
display_title: My landlord billed me $4,200 for a staircase I never touched — and I only found out why yesterday
beats: My landlord charged me $4,200 for 'structural damage' to a staircase I've never once touched with my hands.
I climb it, sure. Every night, in Minecraft, on my phone, filming parkour runs on a course I built in the stairwell of my rented house's basement.
Six months of blocks stacked against real walls, timed jumps synced to real creaks in real wood, my one actual hobby.
Two weeks ago the landlord did a 'routine inspection' while I was at work and saw my setup: laptop stand, ring light, chalk marks on the steps for camera angles.
He texted me a photo of it captioned 'this better not be why my stairs are wearing out.'
I laughed. Blocks in a video game don't wear down real oak.
Yesterday the bill came: $4,200 for 'excessive foot traffic damage,' itemized down to the tread.
I asked for proof. He sent one thing back — a photo of my own filming schedule, taped to my door, that I forgot was still there.
Under it, in his handwriting: 'Found this. Charged you for every night on the list. Should've just asked to watch.'
So, was this really about the stairs, or was he just mad nobody asked him to be in the video?
